title: Turning or positioning for loud breathing without turning it into a countdown

source_packet.source_basis: Public-source practice-layer synthesis for schema testing; no private testimony, no contributor interview, no claim of corpus completeness.
limitations: Public sources describe recognized care patterns but do not supply firsthand room texture.
This record must not become procedure-level instruction for a particular death.
Treatment, legal, ritual, emergency, and equipment decisions remain local and must be handled by qualified teams or relevant authorities.

moment.plain_scene: Noisy breathing frightens the room. A witness asks whether to turn the person, raise the head, call someone, or read the sound as the final countdown.
ordinary_language_queries: turn on side for death rattle
noisy breathing hospice what to do
rattly breathing end of life position

content_layers.observation_text: Public and professional sources describe noisy secretions near death and may mention repositioning or clinical assessment, while also warning against assuming distress or using a sound as a precise timer.
content_layers.source_synthesis: Hospice UK and NCI/Merck-type public sources describe noisy breathing; NICE requires assessment, discussion, possible non-pharmacological and pharmacological options, and monitoring rather than family countdown-making.

interpretation.editor_interpretation: This record protects the archive from treating a sound as a clock. The care move is not “fix the noise”; it is “understand the noise, check comfort, and route concerns.”

what_this_is_not: not a prediction of minutes or hours left
not an instruction to move a fragile person without guidance
not proof the person is drowning or choking
uncertainties: The person’s comfort cannot be inferred from sound alone.
Positioning safety varies with frailty, wounds, equipment, and setting.
Medication and suction questions require local clinical assessment.
content_layers.lay_orientation: A lay surface should say the sound can be frightening to witnesses and should route distress or questions about moving/medication to the care team.
content_layers.practitioner_notes: A practitioner surface should collect explanations that decouple noise from suffering and timing while keeping the family’s fear visible.
language_notes: Avoid metaphors of drowning unless specifically in a sourced reader query.
Never render “death rattle” as a timer.

provenance.provenance_statement: Drafted from named public sources to test the practice layer. It should be reviewed before any public surface uses it.

safety.clinical_boundary: This record is observational/source-indexing only. It is not medical advice, not a prognosis, not a legal instruction, not a ritual authority, and not a substitute for a local hospice, clinician, emergency, legal, cultural, or care team.
safety.safety_notes: Before public use, route through clinical or domain review and ensure any lay surface directs urgent, worried, legal, medication, swallowing, equipment, or body-handling questions to qualified local support.
